name: Energy & Cleantech
targetResearchers: Electrochemists, battery scientists, catalysis researchers, and plasma physicists working on storage, fuels, fusion, and carbon capture
useCases: Battery chemistry licensing from university labs
description: Energy and cleantech companies translate breakthroughs in electrochemistry, catalysis, and plasma physics into batteries, fuels, fusion reactors, and carbon-capture systems. The sector draws talent and IP directly from university labs and DOE national laboratories, and many of its flagship startups began as academic spinouts. Sponsored research and pilot validation with university labs are core to de-risking new chemistries before scale-up.
